title: Prove the width-two F2 six-call floor with genuine group-word collisions
body:
The support-only relaxation in #6048 leaves the five-call `diag([xyx],[yxy])` question open because independently assigned subset classes need not respect group cancellation. This package proves a **computer-assisted six-call floor for arbitrary groups and label sets, restricted to width two over F2**, when the two distinct targets each require at least three labels. For `xyx/yxy` satisfying those hypotheses the direct six-call construction meets the bound.

The proof explains why common-prefix/suffix cancellation and joint coefficient parity preserve every actual group realization. A small exact refutation enumerates all 9,331 rank-one-projector tuples of lengths zero through five, with zero survivors; it does not enumerate groups or infer a theorem from finite-group examples. A written five-call example exposes the shared relation that a support-only relaxation misses.

Validation: registered Python 3.12 normal and optimized checks; independent authentication of every generated cancellation rule; exact six-call endpoint; collision-solver acceptance of known four- and six-call constructions; reopened four-call control without cancellation and reopened two-call control without the short-target restriction; committed-byte, source-history and mode checks; official export/input check; Git-free normal and optimized replay. Exact source heads #6048 `518cd2a7880f94b80c9c93aad304a7f041def647` and #6038 `0cee0e104b68ce6f06bf84af03f46ac30680e64c` are pinned and retained in ancestry without changing frozen files.

Scope: the result depends on the small Python refutation and its written soundness argument. Other fields, larger widths, proof-kernel verification, native tariffs, restoration, complete suppliers and the selected frontier remain outside this result. Open next questions are included.

Credit: Josie Elliston (#6048), Nick Petalas (#6038), Wentao Li (#4089/#4093), and Cinna Davis (#2246). Prepared by JoyboyBrian with substantial OpenAI Codex assistance. Canonical investigation: https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/discussions/6093.
